About the Role We’re hiring an Electrical Engineer to design, build, and test the electronics behind our flight and ground hardware. You’ll report directly to our lead electrical engineer and work daily with our mechanical, embedded software, and systems engineers. This is a generalist seat. One week you’re capturing a schematic and bringing up a new board on the bench. The next, you’re holding a supplier to its statement of work and checking that what ships matches what we specified. This is built for someone a few years into their career who has already put real hardware on a bench and wants a far bigger slice of the system than a large prime can offer. The role is onsite daily at our Ashburn Virginia facility. What You’ll Do - Design and capture schematics for analog, digital, and power boards: sensors, data acquisition, power delivery, and the interfaces between them. - Select components, build BOMs, and see boards through fabrication and assembly. - Bring up new PCBs with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, and bench supplies, then debug and characterize them against requirements. - Support systems engineering on requirements, architecture, and interfaces. - Design and document wire harnesses and interconnects: wire gauge, connectors, pinouts, and interface control documents (ICDs). - Manage electronics

jobs.title: Optics Lab Manager
jobs.description_text: We're in the earliest phase, where every optical experiment that proves out our system is built, aligned, and run by a small, dedicated team. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for an Optics Lab Manager to own our optics lab end-to-end: the space, the equipment, the test setups, and the experiments that run on them. You'll be the hands-on implementation lead for our optics team, turning experimentation goals into lab hardware. Our optics team designs the system. You make it real on the bench. Today, lab bandwidth is the constraint on how fast we learn, and this role removes it. This person sets the pace for the team's progress in the coming months and years. This role reports to our Director of Optics. Our optics team works across three functions: design, experimentation, and fielding; you will own experimentation, the bridge between them. It is a high-autonomy position for an experienced experimentalist: we define the project goals and technical risks as an integrated team, and you derive the experimental setups that retire them. You'll implement repeatable processes while training and mentoring the growing team. You'll also sit on the project team from the earliest design discussions, proposing fast lab tests that answer design questions and feeding results straight back into the design, so we iterate quickly through testing rather than analysis alone. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Turn goals into experiments: translate project goals and technical risks into experiment plans and setups, choos

jobs.title: Structural Dynamics Engineer
jobs.description_text: ABOUT OVERVIEW ENERGY Overview Energy is a mission-driven team committed to building a new layer of energy infrastructure: satellites in geosynchronous orbit that redirect solar energy to terrestrial solar projects via passively safe near-infrared (NIR) light. We're in the earliest phase, where every structure we launch is analyzed, tested, and proven end-to-end by a small, dedicated team. ABOUT THE ROLE We're hiring a Structural Dynamics Engineer to build Overview Energy's structural analysis, verification, and model validation capability from scratch. Every structure we put into orbit has to survive launch and years of thermal cycling. Your analysis is what stands between a design and a satellite that fails silently nearly 36,000 km away. Get it right, and solar farms already on the ground keep producing power after dark. Working daily in our Ashburn, VA office, you'll work alongside our structural, optics, mechanisms, and systems engineering teams. You'll run the simulations, define the tests, build the fixtures, and command the room when the shaker table turns on. Along the way, you'll build the tools, procedures, and test capability this practice runs on for years to come. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Build Nastran models from scratch for the primary structure, deployables, and the structure holding our optics - Own loads and margins of safety for every flight structure, from launch vibration and shock to bolted joints - Deliver Craig-Bampton models to launch providers and interpret

jobs.title: Spacecraft Thermal Engineer
jobs.description_text: We're in the earliest phase, where every thermal path between a multi-kilowatt payload and deep space is designed, built, and tested end-to-end by a small, dedicated team. About The Role We’re hiring a Spacecraft Thermal Engineer to co-own thermal control for our first spacecraft and the GEO platform behind it. This role is built for someone a few years into their career who has already taken a thermal model into a chamber and seen what the test proved wrong. A multi-kilowatt payload in geosynchronous orbit has to shed its heat to deep space through full sun and eclipse, year after year. Your design keeps the optics aligned and the electronics alive nearly 36,000 km from anyone who could fix them. Get it right, and the beam lands exactly where solar farms need it. Based in our Ashburn, VA office, you’ll work alongside our structures, optics, and integration teams. You’ll build the models, run the chamber, and correlate the results yourself. Along the way, you’ll stand up our thermal test capability, carry projects from proposal through test, and write the standards every future spacecraft will use. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Co-own thermal control design for our first spacecraft and GEO platform, from radiator sizing and heater zones to coatings and MLI - Build and correlate Thermal Desktop and SINDA/FLUINT models, running the hot and cold cases, trades, and margins - Deliver optical bench temperature maps to the structures and optics teams for Structural Thermal Optical Performance (S

jobs.title: Deployed Strategist
jobs.description_text: Job: You will own customer outcomes across Parallel's strategic accounts and make retention and expansion a deliberate motion as we scale. You'll define what success looks like with our customers before go-live and build the dashboard tying every metric back to the economic case the GTM team sold against. You'll partner with Deployed Engineering on strategic deployments, build reference architectures for the workloads the customer base is concentrating around, and run a structured operating cadence that turns realized ROI into expansion, renewals, and references the AE team carries into the next deal. You'll also own the customer → product feedback loop, routing usage signals and friction patterns into prioritized input Product can act on. You: Have run post-sale at an infrastructure or AI company and can speak credibly about agent frameworks, background-agent workloads, and how our APIs compose into a real customer workflow. You've defined outcome metrics tied to commercial impact before, and you know the difference between a customer who's using the product and a customer whose ROI is visible enough to expand against. You see expansion whitespace early, you know when a renewal is at risk before the QBR, and you're energized by building the function from scratch rather than inheriting one.

jobs.title: GTM Recruiter
jobs.description_text: Job: You will own full-cycle recruiting for sales at Parallel, running searches from intake through close. You'll partner directly with hiring managers and founders to define role scope, build interview loops, and calibrate what "great" looks like for each role. You'll drive sourcing and outbound for hard-to-fill and senior roles, manage candidates through the pipeline without letting anyone go cold, and help sharpen the scorecards and playbooks the team runs on as headcount scales fast. You'll report on pipeline health and hiring velocity to the recruiting lead, and you'll be trusted to close high-conviction offers on your own. You: Have run full-cycle sales recruiting at an early-stage or fast-growing company and know how to own searches end to end. You can hire AEs in your sleep. You've worked sales and marketing roles and know how to flex your pitch and interview process for each. You write outbound that gets responses from people who aren't looking, and you know how to close a candidate who has three other offers. You work well solo but you're just as sharp coordinating with other recruiters on shared priorities, and you move fast because slow hiring kills momentum at a company this stage.

jobs.title: Product Marketing, Ecosystem Partners
jobs.description_text: Job: You will make Parallel the default web layer for developers and enterprises building AI agents on our partners’ platforms. You’ll own positioning and messaging across our cloud, developer-tool, agent-framework, and services partners: what each integration does, who it’s for, and why it matters. You’ll run joint launches end to end, from narrative and code examples to launch content and the follow-through that turns a launch into adoption. You’ll build enablement that partners’ sales and solutions teams actually use, decide with partnerships, product, and sales which integrations get priority, and own the adoption and pipeline they drive. What you hear from partners and the developers building on them goes straight back into the roadmap. You: Have done partner, ecosystem, or integrations product marketing at an API, infrastructure, or developer-tools company, and can show what a platform launch moved. You’re technical enough to write a code-backed launch post and credible with the engineers who read it. You can write a one-pager that sells, and you can tell a real differentiator from fluff. Experience with cloud marketplaces or open-source agent frameworks is a real advantage. You’d rather ship, learn, and say what you got wrong than polish a deck.

jobs.title: Accounting Manager
jobs.description_text: Job: You will own accounting at Parallel end to end, from month-end close and financial reporting to technical accounting, audits, tax, and statutory compliance. You'll manage multi-entity accounting as Parallel scales internationally, own our relationships with external accounting, tax, and audit partners, and drive the systems and future ERP decisions that support a fast-growing business. You'll partner closely with revenue leadership and the finance lead on quote-to-cash improvements and billing operations, and you'll build the processes and infrastructure that let the accounting function scale without breaking. You: Have 8+ years of accounting experience at a high-growth technology company, with a track record of taking on increasing ownership of the function. You have deep expertise in US GAAP, technical accounting, and SaaS revenue recognition, and you're comfortable with multi-entity and international operations, transfer pricing, and inter-company accounting. You understand billing systems and revenue operations well enough to partner directly with commercial teams, not just report on them after the fact. You're a builder who wants to design the systems, not just operate them, and you stay close to the details even as you take on more scope. Bonus if you've led an ERP migration or can write SQL to answer your own questions instead of waiting on someone else's dashboard.

jobs.title: Strategic Finance
jobs.description_text: Job: You will help shape Parallel’s business and financial strategy as a member of the Strategic Finance team. You’ll partner with leaders across the company, own key financial models, and use your analysis to drive critical company decisions. Projects may span compute analysis, pricing and packaging, unit economics by product, strategic distribution partnerships, and setting up KPIs for the business. You’ll pull data from wherever it lives and set it up for ongoing reporting to the leadership team. Your scope will grow as fast as you earn it. You: You’ve spent a few years in a high-rigor seat like investment banking or strategy consulting, followed by an investing role at a private equity or growth firm, or a finance role at a high-growth company. You’ve built detailed, complex models from first principles, and you can defend every assumption when someone pushes back. You’ve used AI tools to do real work faster, and you’re eager to find new ways to apply them. You take ownership without being asked, flag problems early, and want to grow into a finance and general business leader at Parallel.

jobs.title: Marketing Ops
jobs.description_text: Job: You will own Parallel's marketing systems and the data that runs through them. You'll own the HubSpot and Salesforce integration. Together with Revenue Operations, you'll move us to an account- and contact-based model that sales and marketing both trust. You'll build lead scoring and the attribution model that shows which demand generation actually creates pipeline. With data engineering, you'll rebuild how product data flows from BigQuery into our marketing systems, so the whole team acts on usage signals as well as form fills. You'll run the stack end to end, from enrichment and events to reporting, and build agentic workflows where they beat a manual process. You: You’re a problem-solver and inherently fired up by challenges. You’re curious about new technology and approach it from an experimental mentality. You have bias to action and know how to balance short term progress with longer term systems-building. You've owned the marketing technology stack at a B2B or developer-first company: marketing automation, BI, enrichment, events and the ETL behind them.

jobs.title: Procurement Lead
jobs.description_text: Job: Be a frugal, strategic, and and hard negotiator for Parallel. You will build and lead Parallel's Procurement function as we scale a generational AI infrastructure company. You’ll lead our compute negotiations, one of largest cost centers, structuring commitments with cloud and infrastructure providers that keep pace with fast, hard-to-forecast growth. You’ll own vendor procurement across software, services, and infrastructure, from intake to signature. You’ll also own content and data partnership payouts while are key to enhancing our product performance. You’ll partner closely with finance, accounting, legal, and engineering, and you’ll help hire the team as the function grows. You: You’ve been the first procurement lead at a high-growth tech company and built the function from nothing. You’ve personally negotiated large, complex deals across cloud, AI, data, and software, and you can point to what you won. You understand compute economics: reserved versus on-demand, commit sizing, and the levers that keep things flexible. You’ve owned the full flow from request to contract to payment, so accounting stays clean. You use AI tools to move faster with a lean team. Teams come to you early because you make forecasting, and buying easier, not harder.

jobs.title: Head of Deal Desk
jobs.description_text: Job: You will own how deals get priced, structured, approved and booked at Parallel. As our first Deal Desk hire, reporting into GTM Operations, you’ll build the function from scratch: approval matrices, discount guardrails, quoting workflows and a clear path for non-standard terms, built for usage-based enterprise AI deals. Every non-standard quote, discount request and custom term runs through you, across the full deal lifecycle. You’ll work live deals alongside account executives and sales leadership, and partner with legal and accounting so every deal closes fast, on Parallel’s terms, and books and bills cleanly. You’ll own our CRM and quoting stack, work with Legal on contract management, and build with AI and automation by default. Your deal insights will shape our pricing and packaging. You’ll start deep in deals, then scale the function and team as volume grows. You: Have built or led a Deal Desk at a fast-paced, high-growth company and can show how it made deals move faster, not slower. You’ve structured ramp deals, prepaid commitments and multi-year contracts under consumption or committed-spend pricing, and you know where the risk sits in each. You understand how deal terms flow through to revenue recognition, billing and margin. You can model a deal’s economics in minutes and explain the tradeoffs to an AE at quarter end. You’re senior, but you’d rather work the deal yourself than hand it off. You’ve used AI to cut quote turnaround, run first-pass redlines or auto

jobs.title: GTM Strategic Finance
jobs.description_text: Job: You will be a core part of the Go-to-Market (GTM) Strategic Finance team. You’ll partner directly with revenue leadership on hiring plans, quota and capacity models, compensation plans, and spend. Additionally, you will help inform complex strategic distribution and customer deals. You’ll turn pipeline, attainment, and unit economics into recommendations that impact the sales organization. You’ll build the operating plan and bookings forecast for the sales org and hold it accountable to them. You’ll bring a financial lens to pricing and packaging across usage-based and committed-spend models, and you’ll set the credits and discount policy, as well as margin targets that the deal desk enforces. You’ll work with the broader Corporate Finance team on sales planning and board reporting. As the function grows, you’ll be instrumental, early, contributor and grow with Parallel. You: You’ve spent a few years in a high-rigor seat like investment banking or strategy consulting, followed by an investing role at a private equity or growth firm, or a GTM finance role at a high-growth company. You’ve set sales strategy including quotas, building capacity models, and commission plans alongside sales leaders who trusted your numbers. You’ve used AI tools to do real work faster, and you’re eager to find new ways to apply them. You take ownership without being asked, flag problems early, and want to grow into a finance and general business leader at Parallel.

You’ll partner directly with company leaders on headcount plans, budgets, and the tradeoffs between building, buying and adding compute. You’ll work with Parallel’s procurement lead on compute and vendor negotiations, and with Accounting on how R&D costs are treated and capitalized. You’ll turn cost per query, contribution and gross margin, and infrastructure efficiency into a clear strategy for the company. You: You’ve owned Finance for an engineering or infrastructure organization at a high-growth tech company, ideally one where compute or cloud was a major cost line. You’ll own the campaigns end to end: messaging, channel mix across digital, email, direct mail, events, and executive engagement, and the measurement that proves what worked. You’ll partner with our senior enterprise marketer as a hands-on individual contributor, turning one-off plays into repeatable programs. You’re accountable for account engagement, funnel conversion, and marketing-sourced pipeline. You: Have run ABM and enterprise demand gen at a high-growth B2B technology company, ideally in AI, developer infrastructure, or cloud. You’ve worked inside CRM, marketing automation, intent data, and account intelligence tools, and you use them to segment, target, and measure rather than to report activity. You think in numbers: you know which accounts are warming, which campaigns earned their spend, and why. Your bar for content is high. You write for the channel and the format, you protect the brand’s voice, and nothing you ship reads like AI slop. You use AI-native tools fluently but don’t lean on them for ideas. You can judge whether a control is worth its cost and noise before we buy or build it. You treat corporate security as an engineering problem. You automate checks and fixes through APIs rather than clicking through admin consoles, and you would rather ship a control that covers most of the company this month than a perfect one next year. You will work closely with product, design, and go to market teams, and talk directly with developers to understand where they get stuck. ABOUT YOU: You are a product minded engineer who cares deeply about the people using what you build. You move quickly, care deeply about the details, and measure success by whether developers succeed with the product. jobs.title: Product Marketing, Index
jobs.description_text: Job: You will own positioning and go-to-market for Index, Parallel’s marketplace for the agentic web. Agent builders get grounded access to high-quality content; publishers, data providers, and creators see how agents use their work and earn from what it contributes. You’ll make the case to both sides: to agent builders, from AI-native startups to the largest enterprises, why Index content produces better answers, and to content owners, from news publishers to independent creators, why they should join, what they learn, and how they earn. You’ll lead launches, new content categories, and the move to self-serve, build proof programs with launch partners, and shape the public narrative on how the open web stays sustainable when agents become its largest users, alongside the founding team. You: Have owned positioning for a product line or company and have marketed a two-sided marketplace or platform. You know how to balance supply and demand, and when one side has to come first. Media, data licensing, or usage-based monetization experience is a plus. You ask why until the answer is real.

That means running immigration coordination with outside counsel for roughly 30 visa holders and owning onboarding and offboarding for about 15 new hires a month. You’ll also keep benefits, payroll inputs and employee records in Rippling clean and ready for audit. You’ll be the first person employees come to with questions, and they’ll get fast, accurate answers. As headcount heads toward 150 and new regions come online, you’ll build international onboarding, run open enrollment and handle the logistics of our first performance cycle. You’ll report to the People Ops lead and own the operational side yourself, so they can focus on manager enablement and engagement. You’ve managed H-1B, O-1 or E-3 cases alongside immigration counsel, and you know the timelines cold. You track dozens of moving pieces without dropping one, and you spot the broken step in a workflow the second time you run it. You can explain a benefits plan or a visa timeline in plain language. About you: Have deep intuition on developer tooling, build systems, CI/CD, and AI assisted development. You see software development changing with AI and want to build the tools this new reality needs. You have strong taste in what makes a tool great to use, and you care about understanding what other engineers need and building tools they love. You might be a good fit if you have: - Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education, training, and professional experience - Experience building developer tooling, CI/CD, build systems, or internal platforms that other engineers depend on every day - Hands on experience using AI coding and review agents in your daily workflow, with informed opinions on where they help and where they fall short - A track record of treating engineers as your customers, gathering their input, and driving adoption of tools because they genuinely make work better LIFE AT PARALLEL We believe in a fully in person work culture 5 days a week.

jobs.title: Technical Recruiter
jobs.description_text: Job: You will own recruiting for early career engineering talent at Parallel, hiring new grads and early career engineers across ML, backend, and data roles. You will source from top CS programs, research labs, and early stage startups, and build relationships with the students and engineers who will become the next generation of great builders. You will partner directly with engineering leaders to define role scope, design interview loops, and calibrate what “great” looks like for each profile. You will partner with engineering leaders to calibrate what strong early career talent looks like and keep a fast and thoughtful process for every candidate. You: Have run full cycle technical recruiting at an early stage or fast growing company and know how to own engineering searches end to end. You can speak credibly with ML engineers and researchers about their work, and you know the difference between a strong systems engineer and a strong research engineer. You write outbound that gets responses from engineers who are not looking, and you know how to close a candidate weighing offers from the best AI companies in the world. You are fluent in equity and compensation conversations and comfortable navigating visa and immigration timelines. You work well solo but are just as sharp coordinating with other recruiters on shared priorities, and you move fast because momentum matters at a company at this stage.

jobs.title: Data Partnerships Finance Lead
jobs.description_text: Job: You will own Parallel’s search and data partnerships, and over time the full content and data partnerships function. You’ll set the strategy for which search and data partners we deepen, renegotiate, add, or exit, then structure and negotiate the deals yourself. You’ll negotiate hard on cost, exclusivity, and access so Parallel gets the data our product needs on terms that work for us. You’ll work with engineering and product to understand which data actually moves quality, with finance on deal economics and payments, and with legal on licensing terms. You’ll treat partnerships as a portfolio, diversifying where we’re exposed and going deep where it counts. You: You’ve led data licensing or search partnerships at a major platform and personally negotiated large, complex deals. Ideally you’ve sat on both sides, so you know how content owners value their data and where the leverage really sits. You model deal economics as fluently as you run a negotiation, and you tie every deal to cost and product impact. You keep strong partner relationships without forgetting whose side you’re on, and you’ve walked away from deals that didn’t work. You’re ready to run a function today and grow into leading a broader org.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Core Infrastructure
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: You will build and operate the infrastructure that every system at Parallel runs on. jobs.title: Research Scientist - Post-Training
jobs.description_text: Pluralis Research works on Protocol Learning: training and serving large models in a fully decentralized way on small consumer-grade devices connected via the internet. Despite being dismissed as infeasible, we have made significant advances on this problem, most recently Agora, a permissionless run that pretrained an 8B model from scratch on consumer GPUs spread over the internet, with no single participant ever holding the full weights (tech report https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13332). While many of the core research problems have been solved, Protocol Learning unlocks a series of new challenges. For the mission in full, read A Third Path: Protocol Learning https://pluralis.ai/blog/a-third-path-protocol-learning/. Agora gave us a pretrained 8B model. Post-training is how we make it useful for agentic use-cases. But every post-training stack you've seen assumes a datacenter — synchronous rollouts, fast interconnects, trusted workers. Ours gets none of that. It has to run on consumer GPUs, and Macs spread across the public internet, training a model whose weights no single participant ever holds, with rollouts arriving from a geo-distributed inference pipeline at high latencies. Your primary role is to make RL post-training work here anyway — the algorithms and the system, end-to-end. Our training and inference network is trustless, and the workers are GPUs scattered across the world. Many things can go wrong in this system. An inference worker can return tokens from a cheaper model, or a highly quantized version of the one it's supposed to run. Even with the right model, it can sample with the wrong parameters.
